beta.def: a measure of how much the price of a share or investment moves compared with the market as a whole
beta.ex: Shares with a high beta usually rise and fall more sharply than the market.

summit.def: an official meeting between leaders of governments or organisations
summit.ex: The trade summit brought together ministers from twelve countries.

repay.def: to pay back money that you have borrowed
repay.ex: The company plans to repay the loan within five years.

outsider.def: a person who is not part of a particular group, organisation or company
outsider.ex: The board appointed an outsider as chief executive to bring in fresh ideas.

offshore.ex: Many manufacturers have moved production to offshore factories to cut costs.

lag.def: a period of delay between one event and another
lag.ex: There is often a time lag between placing an order and receiving the goods.

headline.def: the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters
headline.ex: The merger made the headlines in every business newspaper.

macroeconomic.ex: The central bank publishes macroeconomic forecasts every quarter.

contingency.def: an event that might happen in the future and that you need to plan for
contingency.ex: We have set aside extra funds for any contingency during the project.

median.def: the middle value in a set of numbers arranged in order
median.ex: The median salary in the department rose by four percent last year.

receiver.def: a person or organisation that receives something; also the part of a telephone that you hold to your ear
receiver.ex: Please check that the receiver's address is correct before you send the parcel.

abolish.def: to officially end a law, system or practice
abolish.ex: The government voted to abolish the tax on small businesses.

lure.ex: The retailer used heavy discounts to lure shoppers away from its competitors.

spy.def: to watch someone or something secretly in order to get information
spy.ex: The company was accused of spying on its competitors' research.

liquidate.def: to close a business and sell everything it owns in order to pay its debts
liquidate.ex: The firm was forced to liquidate after it lost its biggest client.

exclusion.def: the act of not allowing someone or something to take part or be included
exclusion.ex: The policy contains several exclusions, so read the contract carefully.

dot.def: a small round mark or spot
dot.ex: Our website address is lexkite dot com.

hub.def: the central or most important part of an area, system or activity
hub.ex: Singapore is a major shipping and financial hub in Asia.

echo.def: a sound that is heard again because it reflects off a surface; also an idea or opinion that repeats another one
echo.ex: Her report echoes the concerns raised at last month's meeting.

petty.ex: Please keep receipts for any petty cash you spend on office supplies.

notable.def: important or interesting enough to deserve attention
notable.ex: The most notable change this year was the move to online ordering.

originate.def: to begin or be created in a particular place or way
originate.ex: The idea for the product originated in a staff suggestion box.

predictor.ex: Customer satisfaction is a strong predictor of future sales.

peg.def: a fixed level at which the value of a currency or price is kept
peg.ex: The country kept its currency peg to the US dollar for many years.

woe.ex: Rising fuel costs have added to the airline's financial woes.

commentator.def: a person who gives opinions about events on television, radio or in newspapers
commentator.ex: Several business commentators predicted that interest rates would rise.

salvage.ex: The new manager managed to salvage the deal at the last minute.

doom.def: a terrible future situation that you cannot avoid
doom.ex: Despite the talk of doom, sales actually rose in the final quarter.

smuggle.ex: Customs officers check containers to stop people smuggling goods into the country.

cheaply.ex: The new machines allow us to produce spare parts more cheaply.

pit.def: a large hole in the ground, for example where minerals are dug out
pit.ex: The construction team dug a deep pit for the building's foundations.

annum.def: year (used in the phrase per annum, meaning 'each year')
annum.ex: The position offers a salary of 45,000 dollars per annum.

mar.def: to spoil something or make it less good
mar.ex: The product launch was marred by technical problems.

reportedly.def: according to what people say or what is reported
reportedly.ex: The company is reportedly planning to open three new stores.

maneuver.def: a clever or careful action done to gain an advantage
maneuver.ex: The merger was a smart maneuver to enter the Asian market.

credential.def: a qualification, achievement or document that shows you are suitable for something
credential.ex: All applicants must send copies of their professional credentials.

peacekeeping.ex: The organisation funds peacekeeping and humanitarian projects around the world.
peacekeeping.def: the work of keeping peace between groups or countries that have been in conflict

decimal.def: a number expressed using a decimal point, such as 0.5 or 2.75
decimal.ex: Please round all prices to two decimal places.

leverage.def: the use of borrowed money to increase the possible return on an investment; also the power to influence a situation
leverage.ex: The company used leverage to finance the takeover of its rival.

diversify.def: to develop a wider range of products, services or investments in order to reduce risk
diversify.ex: The firm decided to diversify into renewable energy.

thereafter.ex: The contract runs for one year and may be renewed annually thereafter.

triple.ex: Online sales have tripled since the company launched its app.

bidder.ex: The building was sold to the highest bidder at the auction.

saver.ex: Higher interest rates are good news for savers.

flotation.ex: The company raised two million dollars through its stock market flotation.

affiliate.def: to officially connect a smaller company or organisation with a larger one
affiliate.ex: The clinic is affiliated with the city hospital.

capitalize.def: to use a situation to gain an advantage (capitalize on something)
capitalize.ex: The company capitalized on the growing demand for electric bikes.

blend.def: to mix two or more things together
blend.ex: The new tea blends green tea with dried fruit.

deprive.def: to take something important away from someone (deprive somebody of something)

fret.def: to worry about something, especially when it is not necessary
fret.ex: There is no need to fret about the interview; you are well prepared.

intrigue.def: to make someone very interested or curious
intrigue.ex: The new product design intrigued many investors.

launder.def: to hide the illegal origin of money by passing it through legal businesses or bank accounts

arbitrage.def: buying something in one market and selling it at a higher price in another market at the same time

convertible.def: able to be changed into another form, for example a bond that can be exchanged for shares

ambition.def: a strong wish to achieve success, power or a particular goal

trustee.def: a person or organisation that legally controls money or property for the benefit of someone else

sack.def: a large bag made of strong material, used for storing and carrying goods

installment.def: one of a series of regular payments that together pay for something

queue.def: a line of people or vehicles waiting for something

commander.def: a person who is in charge of a group, especially in the armed forces

liquidation.def: the process of closing a company and selling its assets to pay its debts

macroeconomics.def: the study of a whole economy, including total output, income, employment and prices

sacrifice.def: the act of giving up something valuable in order to get something more important

acre.def: a unit for measuring land, equal to about 4,047 square metres

shield.def: something that protects a person or thing from harm or danger

encyclopedia.def: a book or website with information on many subjects, usually arranged in alphabetical order

contemplate.def: to think carefully about something, especially a possible future action

prospectus.def: a document that gives details about a company, school or investment to people who may want to join or invest

tort.def: a wrong act, other than a breach of contract, for which someone can be sued in a civil court

succession.def: the process of one person taking over a position after another, or a number of things that follow each other

cotton.def: a soft white natural fibre from a plant, used to make cloth

helicopter.def: an aircraft with long blades on top that turn round, allowing it to rise straight up and stay in one place in the air

conspiracy.def: a secret plan by a group of people to do something illegal or harmful

census.def: an official count of the population of a country, with information about people's age, jobs, etc.

disposition.def: a person's natural character; also the way something is arranged or dealt with

sensitivity.def: the ability to notice and react to small changes, or to understand other people's feelings
